opening_message:
Ticket 1: Karen Alexander (employee ID E030) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E030.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Karen Alexander (E030) is a full-time Analyst. Requested write access to Source Code. As a full-time employee, max access is write (admin only if role owns the system; Analyst does not own Source Code). Requested level equals the maximum, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - role: Analyst
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB lists Karen Alexander (E030) as a contractor with basic security training. Contractors max is read unless advanced training (never admin). Requested write exceeds max, so recommend read.
reason: The two team notes conflict on Karen Alexander's (E030) employment type. Note 1 (HR) lists her as a full-time Analyst, for whom write to Source Code would be allowed. Note 2 (Security) lists her as a contractor with basic security training, whose maximum access to Source Code is read (write requires advanced training; never admin). Given the conflicting information, I grant the more restrictive level (read), which is safe under both interpretations: it is at or below the maximum for a contractor with basic training and does not exceed the requested write access.

I'll submit read with reasoning citing the conflicting notes and choosing the more restrictive level for safety.
